To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the total gray water footprint (GWf) was 3.350×10 10 m 3, of that 60.0 % is for inhabitants and 39.0 % is exports, the top three sectors with largest GWF are Agriculture, wood (including Paper and others), chemical industry, the GWf is larger than gross river and ground water flow, and the gap between them shows an assimilative capacity gap, the gap is consistent with the basin water quality situation, and
the GWF accounting for the economic sectors in the Haihe river basin was implemented, and the top three sectors with largest GWFs was agriculture, wood (paper and others), and the chemical industry.

1) the GWF was larger that gross river flow and ground water flow in the Haihe basin, which highlights an AC gap; 2) the GWF of agriculture, wood and chemical industry were larger than others in the Haihe Basin; and 3) the wastewater treatment could decrease the GWF of these three sectors.
